notes: M9.3 documentation-paraphrase evaluation. Each query has one relevant target and an explicit relevance judgment. Queries target equivalent meaning with low lexical overlap, not relation traversal. Freeze this file before embedding inference; do not tune a provider or rewrite judgments in response to measured rankings.
controlledPilot: This is a deliberately bounded controlled pilot, not a representative measure of arbitrary documentation search. Real documentation retrieval may have multiple relevant results per query.
singleRelevantTargetAssumption: Each pilot query has exactly one assigned relevant target so Recall@5 and MRR@5 are unambiguous. This assumption is a corpus design choice, not a claim about documentation retrieval generally.

metricConvention.recallAt5: Queries whose relevant target appears in the first five results divided by all queries; every query has exactly one relevant target.
metricConvention.mrrAt5: Mean of 1/rank for the relevant target in the first five results, or zero when absent.
metricConvention.lowLexicalOverlap: At most 0.25 of distinct query tokens occur anywhere in the target's definition, preferred name, aliases, or id, using the M9.2 tokenizer.
metricConvention.tieBreak: Descending score, then concept id ordinal.

concepts.definition: Services registered with a scoped lifetime are instantiated once per request scope.
A transient service is created anew each time it is requested from the container.
A singleton service shares one instance across all consumers for the application's lifetime.
Repeating an idempotent operation has no additional effect after the first successful call.
An index accelerates row lookup at the cost of extra storage and slower writes.
Grant each process only the permissions required for its task, and revoke access when the task ends.
Preserve a document's original character encoding and byte-order mark when saving edits.
Propagate cancellation through asynchronous work so obsolete operations stop promptly and release resources.

entries.query: How do I make sure a dependency gets a separate instance for each web request?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: the document specifies one instance per request scope, which supplies the requested per-request lifetime.
entries.rationale: Tests the architectural ruling's example without requiring the words scoped or instantiated.

entries.query: Which lifetime keeps one object alive throughout a single HTTP exchange?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: one instance per request scope is the lifetime spanning one HTTP exchange.
entries.rationale: Distinguishes request scope from application-wide sharing and fresh-per-resolution behavior.

entries.query: How can two services share the same dependency during one server-side request without sharing it with other requests?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: one instance per request scope is shared by services within that request and isolated from other requests.
entries.rationale: Tests sharing within a request and isolation across requests without naming the scoped lifetime.

entries.query: Which registration gives me a fresh object whenever something asks for it?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: the document defines creation anew on every container request.
entries.rationale: Paraphrases requested-from-the-container as something asking for an object.

entries.query: How can two consumers receive different instances even during the same operation?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: separate container requests create separate transient instances, even within one operation.
entries.rationale: Contrasts with scoped sharing without naming either lifetime.

entries.query: How can separate components avoid receiving the same dependency instance when they are constructed?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: creating a new transient service for each container request gives separately constructed components distinct dependency instances.
entries.rationale: Expresses fresh-per-resolution through non-sharing between components without naming the transient lifetime.

entries.query: How do I make every part of the program share the same cache object?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: a singleton shares one instance across all consumers for the application's lifetime.
entries.rationale: Describes application-wide sharing without the singleton term.

entries.query: Which setting keeps one shared helper available until the application shuts down?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: a singleton shares one instance across consumers for the application's lifetime.
entries.rationale: Paraphrases application-lifetime sharing as one shared helper available until shutdown.

entries.query: I want every component to use the same configuration-provider instance throughout the application.
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: a singleton provides one configuration-provider instance to all components for the application's lifetime.
entries.rationale: Uses a concrete configuration-provider example to describe application-wide instance sharing.

entries.query: Why can a client safely retry a payment without charging twice?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: no additional effect after the first successful call explains why a retry does not duplicate the charge.
entries.rationale: Concrete payment paraphrase with no idempotency terminology.

entries.query: What property prevents duplicate submissions from applying the same change again?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: idempotency prevents repeated calls from adding effects after the first success.
entries.rationale: Describes the guarantee rather than naming the property.

entries.query: How should an API handle the same operation being delivered twice without applying its effect again?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: an idempotent operation has no additional effect when the same operation is delivered again after its first success.
entries.rationale: Tests duplicate operation delivery against the no-additional-effect guarantee without naming idempotency.

entries.query: How can a database locate matching records more quickly in a very large collection?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: an index accelerates row lookup, which is the documented mechanism for locating matching records faster.
entries.rationale: Paraphrases accelerated row lookup as faster record location in a large collection.

entries.query: What tradeoff makes reads quicker but inserts more expensive?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: the document states faster lookup at the cost of extra storage and slower writes.
entries.rationale: Tests the documented tradeoff using read/insert synonyms.

entries.query: Why does the database take up more space after I optimize searches?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: the index document identifies extra storage as the cost of accelerated lookup.
entries.rationale: Describes the storage cost as increased database space after search optimization, without naming an index.

entries.query: What limits the damage if one component is compromised?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: granting only task-required permissions limits what a compromised component can access.
entries.rationale: Describes the security consequence without naming the principle.

entries.query: How much authority should a background worker receive?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: the document answers that a process should receive only permissions required for its task.
entries.rationale: Paraphrases permissions as authority and process as background worker.

entries.query: Should a program keep powerful access after finishing a job?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: the document says to revoke access when the task ends.
entries.rationale: Tests the revocation clause using job-completion wording.

entries.query: How do I keep the file's original text representation intact while changing its contents?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: preserving encoding and byte-order mark while saving edits preserves the original text representation.
entries.rationale: Paraphrases encoding preservation without using encoding or BOM.

entries.query: What must survive unchanged when a Unicode document is rewritten?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: the original character encoding and byte-order mark must survive the edit unchanged.
entries.rationale: Uses Unicode/rewrite wording rather than the document's preservation terminology.

entries.query: How do I stop a text editor from stripping the invisible marker at the beginning of a file?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: the document requires preserving the byte-order mark when saving edits; the query describes that mark without naming it.
entries.rationale: Paraphrases byte-order mark as an invisible marker at the beginning of a file.

entries.query: How can I abandon a background job when the user navigates away?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: propagating cancellation stops work whose result is obsolete after navigation.
entries.rationale: Describes an obsolete-operation scenario without cancellation vocabulary.

entries.query: What tells an in-flight task to stop after its result is no longer needed?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: cancellation propagation tells obsolete asynchronous operations to stop.
entries.rationale: Paraphrases obsolete operations as results no longer needed.

entries.query: How should obsolete async calls release their handles promptly?
entries.relevanceJudgment: Relevant: the document links cancellation propagation to prompt stopping and resource release.
entries.rationale: Paraphrases asynchronous work and resources while retaining some strong lexical cues.

reviewNotes: Human review approved the 24 target assignments after eight required wording revisions. The fixture is a controlled pilot; relevance judgments must not change in response to embedding results.
